meaning_fix: as written (إجت) this is "if she doesn't come, start without me"; for "if I don't come" the verb must be إجيت ijiit
reasoning: إذا is said iza in urban Palestinian. I followed the English and gave the 1sg ijiit; إجت is the 3fs she came. balshu is the plural imperative of ballash.
Initial hamza seat is written as the vowel: amlas. Accurate Arabic, but a Ramallah speaker says naa3im for smooth and zal7aan or bizla7 for slippery.
ط is emphatic T: Taalib. Everyday word for a school or university student.
ث is a plain t and the vowel is long oo, so respelled تور.
ع is 3 and the shadda doubles the emphatic ض, written as a doubled capital.
Long oo, not uu: loon. Plural alwaan.
Keeps the aw diphthong and has a glottal ق: maw'af. Used for a car park and for a bus or service stop; the same word also means a stance.
7aTT with emphatic T and shadda; يد is iid in Palestinian with the -u possessive. The article assimilates to the sun letter ن.
Instrument noun with shadda doubling the whole sh digraph, and e for the taa marbuta after ف.
kaan laazim plus a bare subjunctive gives the should-have sense. The Palestinian verb is form II khabbar, so akhabbrak rather than MSA akhbirak.
Negative imperative with la plus the 2fs subjunctive. 7aal plus a suffix is the Palestinian reflexive: 7aalik to a woman.
ص is emphatic S and backs the taa marbuta to a: furSa.
راس has no hamza in Palestinian: raasi. فوق has a long oo and a glottal ق: foo'. Said to accept a request as an honour; also heard reduced to 3a raasi.
Glottal ق and a taa marbuta after ر, which gives a: ma'bara.
Past 3ms of rikib with two kasras, plus raas and the Palestinian -u possessive. Literally he rode his head, said of someone who dug his heels in.
The article assimilates to the sun letter س, with a shadda: is-sabt.
The ـاة ending is a stressed long aa, so 7ayaa. Normally said with the article: il-7ayaa.
lamma for past time clauses; kunt for I was. The first vowel of Sghiir drops, and the ص voices to an emphatic z before غ, still written S.
biddi takes the independent object iyyaa plus suffix; the 3ms h is not pronounced after the long vowel.
Distinctively Palestinian causative of raa, to see: warjaani means he showed me. Syrian uses farja instead.
Initial hamza seat written as u; the -iyye ending has a doubled ya. Colloquial Ramallah often says ghinniyye instead.
ya3ni is the all-purpose Palestinian discourse marker. b-present 2ms of 'aSad, with a glottal ق and emphatic S; the ellipsis is not romanized.
Form IV past, initial hamza seat written as the vowel a. Semi-formal but genuinely said in Ramallah, especially with the noun ihaane.
Long oo: khoof, from khaaf, to be afraid.
Initial hamza seat is written as the vowel i, and the medial hamza is written: israa'iil. The parenthetical in the English is confusing, but the name itself is right.
